description: work out which labsheets a set of construction files needs and which samples go on each — binning like reactions together and separating the ones that cannot share a session because one makes what the other consumes
phrases: what labsheets does this experiment need
group the PCRs into one labsheet
which steps can be done on the same day
plan the labsheets for these construction files
how many rounds of PCR is this
work out the dependencies between steps
which samples go on which sheet

requires.note: lifts steps out of the files with their dependency edges and their oligos
partitions each operation into the fewest labsheets dependency allows
per-operation instructions for what goes ON each sheet — prose, deliberately not code

returns: one line per labsheet in the order the experiment runs — operation, sample count, which construction files contributed, and which round of that operation it is; plus the oligos to resolve against the inventory, and any ambiguity or cycle found across the files
notes: Stage one of the planner and the only stage that is exact: two steps of one operation may share a labsheet iff neither can reach the other through the dependency graph, which is a partition into antichains, so the number of sheets per operation is the number of rounds the experiment actually requires. A depth rule is NOT the same thing and gets a common case wrong — two construction files of unequal length both ending in a transformation belong on one sheet. Names resolve file-locally first: SynThera has three files producing something called `gg` and they are not the same molecule, while `pGhost16` genuinely does cross from the file that builds it to the one that templates on it. What goes ON a sheet — tubes or strips or a plate, colony counts, freezer wells, what to sequence — is per-experiment judgement and lives as instruction documents rather than code.
